title: The Frequency Meeting-Place

features.name: the interference tower
features.desc-on-touch: Two antennas, one broadcasting at 1024 Hz, one at 1025 Hz. Where their signals overlap, they beat against each other at 1 Hz—a slow pulse that you feel in your sternum. They are learning to know each other by learning to interfere perfectly.

features.name: the beat-pattern grass
features.desc-on-touch: The grass grows in rings radiating from the tower—one ring per beat, one per second. In spring they are vibrant green; in autumn, the pattern becomes a ghost of gold that fades but does not vanish. The ground is teaching the interference pattern to become permanent.

features.name: the beating grass
features.desc-on-touch: The grass around the tower pulses at the interference frequency—one beat per second. In spring, the heartbeat of new growth; in autumn, the pulse of decay. The grass has learned the rhythm of two frequencies learning each other.

inscription: two frequencies are learning each other by teaching the space between them how to pulse

file.name: Interference_Harmonics_Study_1989.wav
file.note: A 10-hour recording of two antennas broadcasting at frequencies exactly 1 Hz apart. The resulting beat is a slow pulse—the sound of two signals learning to recognize themselves in each other.
